concept.title: Docs project layout
concept.shortdesc: A docs project is a folder, usually a whole Git repository, with opend.config.yaml at its root. Copy templates/docs-starter to start one.

conbody.p: Only opend.config.yaml and the root map it names are required. The rest is convention, and the starter template follows it:

strow.stentry: Release, root map, publications, declared attribute values, build filter and theme. See .
The site map, bookmaps for PDF publications, and submaps such as shared key definitions.
One topic file per page. The page URL is the file path without its extension, for example /topics/install.html.
Reusable chunks pulled in with conref or conkeyref. Kept out of every map, so they are never published on their own.
SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP files that topics reference.
The build-time filter, for example to drop audience="internal" for everyone.
Brand colours and fonts for the site, the help panel and PDFs.
Sample readers for the previewer. See .
Maps host-app routes to context-sensitive help keys. See .

ul.li: Files ending in .dita, .ditamap, .bookmap, .ditaval, .xml, .yaml and .yml are read as text. Other files are only checked for existence until something references them.
Folders named .git, node_modules, .opend and dist are ignored.
.xml files whose root is not a topic are left alone, so other XML can live in the project.
Paths in maps, references and the config must stay inside the docs root.
